config.title: Component Composition

intro.title: Component Composition
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user profile card by combining smaller, reusable React components. You will learn component composition, which is the practice of assembling complex UIs from simpler, independent pieces. The main technologies involved are React components, JSX syntax, and props for passing data. By the end, you will understand how to structure applications by nesting components to create maintainable and scalable code.
intro.usecase: Component composition is the foundation of building complex, maintainable user interfaces in modern web applications. For example, a social media dashboard might compose a main feed component from smaller, reusable components like a post card, a comment section, and a reaction bar. Similarly, an e-commerce product page is typically assembled from a product image gallery, a description panel, an 'add to cart' button, and a review list, each managed independently. This pattern allows developers to break down large features into manageable pieces, making the code easier to debug, test, and update as requirements change.

objectives: Construct a parent component that renders multiple child components
Implement props to pass data from parent components to child components
Apply component composition to build complex UI structures from simple building blocks
Configure components to accept and render children using the children prop
Manipulate component hierarchies by nesting components within each other
Integrate composed components within a React application structure
Render dynamic content by composing components with different data inputs

steps.title: Import React
steps.instruction: At the top of the file, import React from 'react' to enable JSX and component creation.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React into your file. This is required for writing JSX.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library
import React from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React is imported and ready to use for creating components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing React specifically from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look like the correct import statement. Remember to import React from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty <div> element.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns JSX containing a div.
steps.seedCode:
import React from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: A component named App is created and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you define a component named App that returns a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named App that returns a div element.

steps.title: Create a Header component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Header that returns a <header> element containing an <h1> with the text 'My App'.
steps.hint: Define a new function called Header that returns JSX with a header and h1 tag.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Header component is defined and ready to be used in the App component.
successCriteria: Header component is created as a function that returns a header element with an h1 containing 'My App'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but check that it returns exactly a header element with an h1 containing 'My App'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Header component wasn't created correctly. Make sure to define a function named Header that returns the required JSX.

steps.title: Create a Content component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Content that returns a <main> element with the text 'This is the main content area.' inside it.
steps.hint: Define a new function called Content that returns JSX. The <main> element should contain the text as a child.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Content component is defined that renders a <main> element with the specified text.
successCriteria: The Content component is created as a function that returns a <main> element containing the text 'This is the main content area.'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the Content component, but make sure it returns a <main> element with the exact text 'This is the main content area.' inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Content component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named Content that returns a <main> element containing the text.

required: This is the main content area

steps.title: Create a Footer component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Footer that returns a <footer> element containing copyright text, such as '© 2024 My App. All rights reserved.'
steps.hint: Define a function called Footer that returns JSX with a footer tag and text inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Footer component is defined and ready to be used in the App.
successCriteria: A Footer component function exists and returns a footer element with copyright text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named Footer and returns a footer element with text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Footer component is not correctly defined. Ensure you create a function named Footer that returns a footer element containing text.

steps.title: Compose components in App
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, render the Header, Content, and Footer components.
steps.hint: Place each component as a JSX element in the return statement, one after another.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now renders the Header, Content, and Footer components as children.
successCriteria: Header, Content, and Footer components are rendered inside the App component's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've rendered some components, but make sure to include all three: Header, Content, and Footer.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component should render the Header, Content, and Footer components inside its return statement.

steps.title: Add props to Header component
steps.instruction: Modify the Header component to accept a title prop and use it inside the header element.
steps.hint: Add a parameter to the Header function to receive props, then use that prop inside the JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Header component will be configurable via a title prop, making it reusable with different titles.
successCriteria: Header component accepts a title prop and uses it inside the header element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the Header function accepts a title prop and uses it in the JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Header component still doesn't accept or use a title prop. Try adding a parameter and using it inside the header.

steps.title: Pass props to Header from App
steps.instruction: In the App component, pass a title prop to the Header component with the value 'My App Header'.
steps.hint: Add the prop directly to the Header component JSX tag in App's return statement.
steps.analogousExample:
// Passing a prop to a child component
<Greeting message="Hello, world!" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component passes a title prop to Header with the value 'My App Header'.
successCriteria: Header component receives a title prop with value 'My App Header' from App.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're passing a prop named 'title' with the exact value 'My App Header' to the Header component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Header component should receive a prop called 'title' with the value 'My App Header' from the App component.

steps.title: Create a Button component with children prop
steps.instruction: Create a new functional component named Button that accepts a children prop and renders them inside a button element.
steps.hint: Define a function called Button that takes props as a parameter, then return a <button> element with {props.children} inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Button component that can wrap any content passed as children inside a button element.
successCriteria: Button component is defined, accepts children prop, and returns a button element containing children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your Button component accepts children and renders them inside a button element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named Button that returns a button with children inside.

steps.title: Use Button component with children in Content
steps.instruction: Inside the Content component, add the Button component and pass text content as children.
steps.hint: Place the Button component inside the Content component's return statement and provide text between its opening and closing tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Content component will render a Button with text content inside it.
successCriteria: Button component is used inside Content component
Button receives text content as children
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the Button is placed inside the Content component's return statement and has text between its tags.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component is not properly used inside Content. Check that it's placed within the Content component and has text content.
